query: What features can be extracted to train a model to predict a review's score?

per_column.name: sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: Sentiment is the single strongest predictor of review score; a 4-way polarity is more informative than a bare positive/negative flag. Sample readings (positive for praise, negative for mislabeled peanuts, mixed for the medicinal cherry soda) are well grounded in the text.

per_column.name: product_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: A quality ordinal gives a genuine axis correlated with score and is only partially redundant with sentiment. Values are sound readings (good, poor, excellent). 'acceptable' for the medicinal soda is a defensible inference though somewhat generous.

per_column.name: taste_flavor_quality
per_column.rationale: Food-specific flavor appraisal is a distinct and useful axis for this food-review dataset. Extractions (delicious, unpleasant medicinal, flavor_mismatch for wrong peanuts) track the text well; NULL used appropriately when taste is not discussed.

per_column.name: product_effectiveness_or_functionality
per_column.rationale: Effectiveness is a plausible predictive axis but 'works_as_claimed' dominates heavily (7174) and is often asserted where the text says nothing about function—e.g. the confection review and taffy review are labeled works_as_claimed with no functional claim in the source. This inflates a default and weakens groundedness.

per_column.name: price_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Price/value perception is a real driver of satisfaction and thus a useful feature. Groundedness is strong: 'good_value' for the great-price taffy, and correct 'Unknown' for rows silent on price (peanuts, cherry soda). Note the dog-food row was labeled good_value despite no price mention—a minor over-assertion.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repurchase intent correlates with score and is a distinct axis. However it is frequently inferred rather than stated: 'will_repurchase' for the confection/taffy rows reflects positive sentiment more than any explicit intent, so values partly restate polarity and over-specify silent rows.

per_column.name: comparison_to_alternatives
per_column.rationale: Whether a review compares to alternatives is a useful, non-redundant feature with a large 'no_comparison' class handled sensibly. Sample labels are mostly grounded, though 'better_than_alternatives' for the dog-food ('better than most') is warranted while the taffy label is a weaker inference.

per_column.name: health_dietary_concern
per_column.rationale: Relevant for a food dataset and offers a distinct dietary axis, but it is near-constant here (no_concern dominates ~6410) limiting leverage. Values are well grounded—no_concern correctly applied to all samples where diet/health is not raised.

judge.rationale: The added columns give multiple genuine, largely non-redundant axes (sentiment, quality, flavor, value, comparison, repurchase, health) that would materially help predict review score, going well beyond trivial length/token flags. Groundedness is generally good with appropriate NULL/Unknown handling for silent rows. The main weaknesses are default-heavy columns—effectiveness ('works_as_claimed') and repurchase intent—where a dominant value is asserted even when the source text does not explicitly support it, and health_dietary_concern is near-constant, reducing its analytical leverage. No hard hallucinations of invented facts were observed; over-assertions are the primary concern.
